extension.description: VBScript for Windows: IntelliSense for COM objects, diagnostics, a debugger, a cscript-compatible script host and a code library.
config.languageServer.path: Path to `VbsTools.LanguageServer.exe`. Empty: use the server bundled in the extension (`server/`).
config.languageServer.trace: Log every completion request in the *VBScript Language Server* output channel (for diagnosing problems). Restart the server after changing it.
config.format.keywordCase: Case of keywords and names when formatting (Shift+Alt+F).
config.format.keywordCase.pascal: Format Document also writes keywords and built-ins in their usual case (End If, MsgBox, vbCrLf) and every use of a script name like its declaration.
config.inlayHints.parameterNames: Show parameter names at calls with two or more arguments, e.g. `fso.OpenTextFile("a.txt", IOMode: 8, Create: True)`. VS Code's `editor.inlayHints.enabled` also applies.
config.inlayHints.parameterNames.literal: Before literal arguments (numbers, strings, True/False, constants), where a name helps most.
config.codeLens.references: Show *N references* above procedures and classes.
config.run.host: Which host runs scripts (`VBScript: Run Script`, Ctrl+F5, the Run button). The VbsTools Script Host behaves like cscript (verified against it) and writes UTF-8, so any characters show correctly in the output panel. Debugging (F5) always uses the VbsTools Script Host.
config.run.host.vbstools: VbsTools Script Host: hosts vbscript.dll itself (the base of the debugger). Preview.
config.run.console: Where `Run Script` shows the output. Also the default for debugging (F5) without a `console` in `launch.json`.
config.run.console.auto: Output panel, errors in the Problems panel; a terminal when the script uses WScript.StdIn.
config.run.console.output: Always the output panel (WScript.StdIn is at its end).
config.run.console.terminal: Always a terminal (input works; errors are links in the terminal).
config.run.scriptHostPath: Folder containing `x64\VbsTools.ScriptHost.exe` and `x86\VbsTools.ScriptHost.exe`. Empty: the host bundled in the extension (`server/host`).
config.run.platform: 64-bit or 32-bit host: `x64`, or `x86` for COM components registered only for 32-bit (cscript from SysWOW64, or the x86 VbsTools host).
config.debug.engine: Debugger engine: `auto` (default) uses the Process Debug Manager (pdm.dll, installed with Visual Studio or Office) when it is available and instruments the script otherwise; `instrumentation` instruments the script and works everywhere; `pdm` always asks for the Process Debug Manager, which also stops at runtime errors with the variables intact, can pause loops without statements and shows the real call stack.
config.debug.trace: Log every Debug Adapter Protocol message to the *VBScript Debug Trace* output channel (for diagnosing the debugger).
config.encoding.ansi: Code page of `.vbs` files without BOM that are not UTF-8 (ANSI), as cscript and wscript read them. `auto`: the system ANSI code page (for example GBK on Simplified Chinese Windows, Shift JIS on Japanese Windows). Such files are reopened with this code page when VS Code shows them garbled.
config.encoding.check: Warn when a script's encoding would make cscript and wscript read its text wrong (UTF-8 with non-ASCII text, UTF-8 with BOM), with quick fixes that save it as UTF-16 LE or ANSI.
config.library.samplesFile: VbsEdit's samples file (`samples2.dat` / `samples.dat`) shown under **Samples** in the Code Library view. Empty: found in the VbsEdit installation folder, else the samples of VbsTools Studio are shown.
config.environments: Host applications whose objects every script can use, e.g. `["WinCC"]` (WinCC V7/V8: `HMIRuntime`, `Item` in event procedures). A single script can also say `' @environment WinCC`. Your own `*.vbstypes.json` files in the workspace apply automatically.
config.typeFiles: More type definition files (`*.vbstypes.json`) or folders, absolute or relative to the workspace folder. They describe objects of applications that run VBScript and have no registered type library.
debug.launch.cwd: Working directory. Default: the script's folder.
debug.launch.console: Where the script's output goes. Default: as `vbscript.run.console` — a terminal when the script uses WScript.StdIn, else the Debug Console.
debug.launch.console.internalConsole: Debug Console (no input: WScript.StdIn is at end of stream).
debug.launch.console.integratedTerminal: VS Code terminal (WScript.StdIn reads from it).

walkthrough.title: Get Started with VbsTools
walkthrough.description: Write, run and debug VBScript with IntelliSense for COM objects.
walkthrough.newScript.title: Write a first script
walkthrough.newScript.description:
Save a sample script and try IntelliSense: type `fso.` to see the members of FileSystemObject, or `CreateObject("` to see the ProgIDs of this computer.
[Create a Sample Script](command:vbscript.walkthrough.newScript)
walkthrough.run.title: Run it
walkthrough.run.description:
Press Ctrl+F5. The output appears in the VBScript panel, errors in the Problems panel.
[Run Script](command:vbscript.run)
walkthrough.debug.title: Debug it
walkthrough.debug.description:
Set a breakpoint with F9 and press F5: step through the script, look at variables and evaluate expressions in the Debug Console.
[Start Debugging](command:vbscript.walkthrough.debug)
walkthrough.library.title: Explore the Code Library
walkthrough.library.description:
Samples to insert or to start from, and your own snippets with shortcuts.
[Open the Code Library](command:vbscript.library.focus)
walkthrough.environment.title: Scripts inside WinCC and other applications
walkthrough.environment.description:
Turn on a host environment for objects such as WinCC's HMIRuntime, or describe your application's objects in a type definition file.
[Choose Environments](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22vbscript.environments%22%5D)
[About Type Definition Files](command:vbscript.openDocumentation?%5B%22type-files.md%22%5D)
walkthrough.attach.title: Debug scripts inside Altium DXP and other applications
walkthrough.attach.description:
Attach to an application that runs VBScript itself: set up the Machine Debug Manager once, then debug from VS Code.
[Check Attach Debugging Environment](command:vbscript.checkAttachEnvironment)
[Open launch.json](command:workbench.action.debug.configure)
walkthrough.docs.title: Read the user guide
walkthrough.docs.description:
Running, debugging, file encodings, settings and answers to common questions.
[Open Documentation](command:vbscript.openDocumentation)
debug.attach.process: Name (or part of the name) of the application to attach to, as the Machine Debug Manager lists it: the path of its executable, e.g. `DXP.exe` for Altium DXP. The application must start after `mdm.exe` is registered.
debug.attach.platform: Script host to use. `x86` for 32-bit applications such as Altium DXP 2004.
debug.attach.stopOnEntry: Stop at the first statement of every script the application runs.
debug.attach.takeOver: When another debugger that is alive is connected to the application, disconnect it and connect this one instead. Altium DXP connects one of its own when a script starts, so attaching to a script that already runs needs this. Off by default, because the other debugger may be somebody's at work.
debug.snippet.attach.label: VBScript: Attach to Altium DXP
debug.snippet.attach.description: Debug the scripts that run inside Altium DXP
debug.attach.environments: Environments (type definition files) that describe the objects of the application, e.g. `["Altium"]`. Used to show the members of objects the debugger cannot expand by itself. Default for `DXP.exe`: `Altium`.
config.attach.checkOnStartup: When the extension starts, check whether attach debugging (`"request": "attach"`) can work on this machine (Process Debug Manager, Machine Debug Manager, group *Debugger Users*) and show a notification if it cannot. The command **VBScript: Check Attach Debugging Environment** runs the same check.
